scenario: Owner's own pending_approval listing fetched with NO Authorization header (token omitted entirely) - owner-check never runs, falls through to the anonymous 404 gate
req_body: GET /listings/cmw9clny500j3u4pwwnlj09tb with no Authorization header sent at all (simulates a client that forgets to attach the owner's token, e.g. the ResumeDraft.tsx pattern applied to a pending_approval listing)
expected: 404 'Listing not found' for the owner's own pending_approval listing when no Authorization header is sent - the server cannot distinguish this request from an anonymous one (BRI-781)
title: Listings Controller find By Id -  Verify a draft or removed listing is not visible to any user other than its owner or an Admin.
preconditions: pending_approval fixture cmw9clny500j3u4pwwnlj09tb, owned by the ST_USER account (role 'user' per fixtures.json _owners); request sent with the Authorization header omitted entirely (not an invalid/expired token - absent)
steps: GET /listings/cmw9clny500j3u4pwwnlj09tb with no Authorization header sent at all (simulates a client that forgets to attach the owner's token, e.g. the ResumeDraft.tsx pattern applied to a pending_approval listing)
business_outcome: Confirms BRI-781: the owner-check (viewer.id === sellerId) at listings.service.ts:784-788 can only run if req.user is populated, which OptionalJwtAuthGuard only does when a valid Authorization header is present. Omitting the header on the owner's OWN pending_approval listing therefore falls through to the exact same 404 gate as a true anonymous caller - a legitimate owner is denied access to their own listing. This is distinct from TC-038-044 (CS:resume-draft-no-token), which only exercises a no-token request against a 'draft' listing; draft is never gated (Finding #1), so that case cannot exercise the owner-check at all and cannot reveal this bug. Only pending_approval (the one status the owner-check actually guards) demonstrates it.
